newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon economic activity up in March.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon economic activity up in March.

text.p: Lebanon's economic activity picked up in March after falling in February to its lowest level in 10 months, the Bank of Lebanon said on Tuesday.

The central bank said in its monthly bulletin that its coincident indicator of economic activity for March stood at 166.0, the level it was at in January before dropping in February to 161.2. This compared with 158.3 in March 1996.
Since the weighting of the 12 economic series included in the indicator is not known, economists question its level of representation of the economy.

The central bank said the number of construction permits issued in March fell 28.2 percent on March 1996. "However, reflecting seasonal activity it (construction) increased by 49 percent relative to February," it said.
The number of new industrial firms, their number of employees, and their registered capital decreased 13.1 percent, 17.2 percent and 53.5 percent respectively on a year-on-year basis, the bank said.
The balance of payments registered a surplus of $564.5 million in the first quarter compared with a surplus of $29.4 million during the same period of 1996.
This reflected "persisting and important capital inflows and remittances, despite the continuing decline in Lebanese pound and treasury bill interest rates", the bank said.
